record.paper_title: Optimal scaling of average queue sizes in an input-queued switch: an open problem
record.original_question: For the same n by n input-queued switch model restricted to uniform traffic, where every input-output arrival rate is λ_i,j = ρ/n, what are the corresponding optimal and maximum-weight-policy queue-size scaling exponents for steady-state expected total queue size as functions of n and ρ, and do the β*_0, β*_1, and β*_2 questions have value 1 in this uniform-traffic case?

evidence.quote: In a further variation, the same questions can be posed for the case of uniform traffic, where λi,j = ρ/n, for all i and j.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a discrete-time n×n input-queued switch. At each time slot, for each input-output pair (i,j) with i,j∈{1,…,n}, packets arrive according to independent Bernoulli processes of rate λ_{i,j} = ρ/n, where ρ∈(0,1). Arrivals at input i are buffered in separate virtual output queues Q_{i,j}(t) per destination j. In each slot, the scheduler chooses a matching σ (a permutation of {1,…,n}) and serves one packet from each queue Q_{i,σ(i)} (if nonempty). The system is stable for any ρ<1.

Let E_π[Σ_{i,j} Q_{i,j}] denote the steady-state expected total queue size under scheduling policy π, viewed as a function of n and ρ.

(a) Determine the optimal scaling exponents β*_0, β*_1, β*_2 defined by
    inf_π lim sup_{ρ→1} (1-ρ)^{β*_0} · lim sup_{n→∞} n^{-β*_1} · E_π[Σ Q_{i,j}]
(and analogous formulations involving joint limits in n and ρ giving exponents β*_0, β*_1, β*_2 governing the dependence on n, on 1/(1-ρ), and on cross terms), restricted to the uniform-traffic regime λ_{i,j}=ρ/n.

(b) Determine the corresponding exponents β_0^{MW}, β_1^{MW}, β_2^{MW} when π is restricted to the maximum-weight matching policy.

(c) In particular, is it true that in the uniform-traffic case all three exponents β*_0, β*_1, β*_2 equal 1 (i.e., the optimal expected total queue size scales as Θ(n/(1-ρ)) up to logarithmic factors), and likewise for the maximum-weight policy?
artifact.status_search_result: For the uniform-traffic n×n input-queued switch, the conjecture is that the optimal expected total queue size scales as Θ(n/(1-ρ)) (i.e., β*_0=β*_1=1). This remains open in full generality, but substantial progress has been made: the conjectured scaling was first established only when 1-ρ=O(1/n²); subsequent work (Maguluri–Srikant; Shah–Walton–Zhong; and later improvements via graph factorization by Maguluri et al., 2019) progressively improved upper bounds, the most recent achieving O(n(1-ρ)^{-4/3} log(max{1/(1-ρ),n})) under uniform arrivals. The tight Θ(n/(1-ρ)) bound (and the corresponding question for the MaxWeight policy) has not been fully proved.

status_evidence.title: Improved queue-size scaling for input-queued switches via graph factorization
status_evidence.snippet: New class of scheduling policies provides expected total queue size scaling as O(n^{1.5}(1-ρ)^{-1} log(1/(1-ρ))) when 1-ρ=O(1/n), improving the state of the art.
status_evidence.claim: Progress on optimal scaling in uniform traffic case; not yet resolved at Θ(n/(1-ρ)).

status_evidence.title: On Queue-Size Scaling for Input-Queued Switches
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the conjecture in the regime 1-ρ=O(1/n²) for uniform traffic.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture proved only in restricted regime.

status_evidence.title: Heavy Traffic Queue Length Behavior in a Switch Under the MaxWeight Algorithm
status_evidence.snippet: MaxWeight has optimal heavy-traffic queue length scaling when all ports are uniformly saturated, within factor 2 of optimal in n.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results for MaxWeight under uniform traffic.
